title: Sunderland 1-1 Jagiellonia Bialystok: Roefs impresses in end-to-end draw
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutSunderland 1-1 Jagiellonia Bialystok: Roefs impresses in end-to-end drawShareSunderland had their chances to win against Jagiellonia Bialystok, but Robin Roefs also helped prevent a defeat in the Europa League.Sunderland were held to a 1-1 draw at the Stadium of Light by Jagiellonia Bialystok in the Europa League.

Tymur Tutierov saw his opener quickly cancelled out by Kamil Jozwiak, and though Regis Le Bris' side had chances to snatch all three points, they also saw Robin Roefs make crucial saves at the other end.
Chris Rigg saw an effort blocked after just 39 seconds, while Enzo Le Fee forced a save from Slawomir Abramowicz shortly after as Sunderland started on the front foot.

The Black Cats then squandered a golden opportunity just before the half-hour mark, with Nilson Angulo seeing a shot blocked on the line by Yuki Kobayashi after Le Fee pounced on a poor pass from Bernardo Vital and rounded the goalkeeper.

Trai Hume flashed wide on the stroke of half-time, but Sunderland were ahead 92 seconds after the restart as Tutierov headed in from a yard out, after Le Fee's cross was deflected goalward by Taras Romanczuk.

However, Jagiellonia were level five minutes later as Jozwiak intercepted a back pass from Reinildo Mandava and rounded Roefs before scoring, and the winger almost repeated the trick on the hour after a loose pass from Jules Ahoka, though Roefs tipped wide on that occasion.
Abramowicz was equal to a weak shot from Rigg before Roefs was called into action by Jesus Imaz, while both Reinildo and Angulo failed to take good opportunities in a crowded box late on.

The best chance for a winner fell to Jeremy Agbonifo, when he wrestled past Thomas Meunier and went through on goal, but rather than squaring to Nic Prelec, he went for goal himself and saw his attempt repelled by Roefs.

After defeating Chelsea and holding Aston Villa to a draw in the Premier League, Sunderland would have hoped to return to winning ways in the Europa League, but they were instead booed off by their fans.

Sunderland's 16 shots, which amounted to 2.15 expected goals (xG), are their lowest total in a Europa League match this season, though they still managed to create three Opta-defined big chances, despite just scoring from one.
Sunderland have scored just eight goals in their opening 10 home games across all competitions this season, their fewest at this stage of a campaign since 2005-06 (also eight).

And no Premier League side have made more errors leading to opposition goals across all competitions this season than Sunderland (eight, level with Aston Villa), a total which could have been the outright most, if not for Roefs.
The Sunderland shot-stopper made four saves in total, the most important coming in the first minute of second-half stoppage time, as the Black Cats goalkeeper at least ensured a point for his side.
Nevertheless, Sunderland have now gone three successive major European matches without a win for the first time (D2 L1), having won five of their first six such games (L1).
